note: v1, SMALL CHANGE: THE RULE, A SKELETON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 04:20-04:45 GMT). Not heard by me. THE RULE (the coin problem): almost nothing is written: a bass drum, a bass and one seed, a single struck note every bar or two (100 in the song); 122, G minor, 192 bars (6:18). Everything else is change given for it. A pair of coins is two echoes, p and q sixteenths long, that feed themselves and each other; each pass through p lifts the sound a fifth (+7), each pass through q drops it a fourth (-5). An echo passed a times through p and b times through q lands p*a + q*b sixteenths after its seed, 7*a - 5*b semitones from it, on the side of its last coin. With 3 and 5 the amounts 1, 2, 4 and 7 cannot be made and from 8 on every sixteenth can, so a seed is answered by a few notes and then a roll; five steps of fifths from B flat are G minor's five notes. The form changes the coins (3 and 5; 3 and 4, which fill from 6; 5 and 7, sparse to 23), how often and where in the bar the seed falls, and its note (B flat, E flat, F). THE EFFECTS: six buses with `returns` from a seed track, themselves and each other, the engine's `pitch` in each loop. MEASURED on the first seed: the echoes sound within 0.9 semitone of the lattice out to sixteenth 21; the first two are 2 dB under the seed, sixteenths 6 to 10 another 6 to 12 dB down, the roll from 11 on 12 to 30 dB under the first two. SCORE 96.12 on both seeds (structure 83.3, 7 sections; spectrum 96.0). ENGINE, LEARNED: `pitch` is late, about 14 ms a pass up a fifth and 18 ms down a fourth with its default grain (3 to 5 ms with grain 10ms, tens of ms and wandering with 80ms), so each return's time is written in ms with the lateness taken off (19.7 / 23.8 ms); the change then peaks between 14 ms before and 23 ms after its sixteenths. The loop loses about 4 dB a pass beyond its gain: at 0.33 the change was gone in three echoes, 0.62 is used. A return hears its track after the fader. EIGHT BUILDS (83.0 the first; the seeds were 14 dB under a mix that was all drum). WHAT IS WEAK: the sections with no drum are 11 to 12 dB under the rest (a fader ride of 6 dB bought 1.9 and was taken out); the timing scatter of the change is the pitch effect's, not a choice; steps six and on round the fifths leave the key (E, B) and are only quiet, not gone; 10 dB under the album's envelope at 14.8 kHz. I cannot judge whether the roll reads as the seed's change or as a separate part, nor whether the scatter sounds loose or wrong.
next: v2 on, every change behind a switch (v1 has one knob, ALONE, at 0). (1) THE NUMBERS SHOULD DRIVE MORE THAN ECHOES (the slot's brief): a filter on each purse whose period is its coins' product in sixteenths (15, 12, 35), a phaser whose rate is p against q, the loop gain ridden so a purse fills over a section. (2) THE OPENING AND THE BREAK are 11 to 12 dB under the rest: a second seed voice or a denser pair there, not a fader. (3) TIMING: try `grain 10ms` on the loops (3 to 5 ms a pass, steadier) and read whether the pitches still follow the lattice; or keep the scatter and say it is the song's swing. (4) THE KEY: steps six and on (E, B natural) are 30 dB down but there; a low-pass that closes with each pass, or seeds whose sixth step is in the key. (5) A CHORD AS THE SEED (the dub stab): every coin then moves the whole chord a fifth. (6) THE TOP: 10 dB short at 14.8 kHz; the loops' low-pass is 10 kHz. (7) The drum and bass are Least Common's, placeholders: give this song its own. v2, THE COINS DO MORE THAN ECHO (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 06:53-07:08 GMT). Not heard by me. Three switches (--without-hat, -debts, -till; all three off is v1 byte for byte) and one left off for an ear (--with-denser). (1) THE HAT PLAYS WHAT CAN BE PAID: counting sixteenths from where the seed falls, a hat on every amount the section's two coins can make, softer the more coins it takes (3 and 5: . . . X . X x . x - x - , - , -). The bar fills like a till; each pair has its own pattern. With the drum come the two coins alone, with the bass everything they can pay. (2) THE BASS PLAYS WHAT CANNOT: the amounts no number of the two coins makes (3 and 5: 1 2 7; 3 and 4: 1 2 5; 5 and 7: 1 2 3 6 9 11 13), never with the drum, the largest a tone lower. Hat and bass never share a sixteenth. (3) Where the seed is off the beat (bars 129-160) hat and bass are counted from sixteenth 6 too: the whole till turns against the drum and comes home with the seed. (4) THE TILL: a low-pass inside each purse's loops sweeps 1.5 to 10 kHz once in p x q sixteenths (15, 12, 35). Seed and coins alone carry 11.5 dB less above 4 kHz in the median sixteenth than without it, at the same level. SCORE 96.60 on both seeds; v1 re-read on the same pin today 96.12. Spectrum 96.0 to 100: v1 was 10.4 dB short at 14.8 kHz, now nothing is more than 5 dB off the envelope (the hat is 99 to 100% of 4 to 16 kHz, 12 to 13.5 dB under the mix). Structure 83.3 (7 sections), variety, recurrence as before. SIX BUILDS: four of them had the opening and the break struck every two bars or every bar, because rendering the seam from Hearing Things showed two bars in every four of the opening are silent (under -56 dB: a seed, two bars of echo, nothing). All four read 88.33: with the opening filled the scorer stops counting the drum's entry at bar 17 as a section (novelty 0.10 to 0.12 against 0.19 sparse; 6 sections, under its range). So DENSER is in the code and off. WHAT IS WEAK: that opening, and the same in the break (bars 81-96): eight seconds in every sixteen with nothing sounding. In the mix the last two bars before the drum fall to -41 and -50 dB. The till's sweep itself I did not isolate: I measured that the echoes are darker, not that they open and shut every 15 sixteenths. The hat's and bass's turn at bar 129 reads 0.07 on the scorer's curve: it may be too small a change to hear as a section. I cannot judge whether the silence in the opening is a pause before the drum or a hole, nor whether the hat reads as arithmetic or as a busy hat.
next: v3 on, every change behind a switch (v2 has hat, debts, till on; denser off). (1) THE OPENING AND THE BREAK: two silent bars in every four. `--with-denser` strikes every bar, 6 dB softer, and reads 88.3 (the scorer loses the drum's entry). Better than either: let the purse ring four bars there (a second pair of loops for those sections with more given back each pass, G about 0.8), so one seed fills its four bars and the drum still arrives as an event. Ask an ear only if that cannot be measured to work. (2) THE TILL: isolate the sweep (a bench: one seed, level above 4 kHz per sixteenth over 35) and make it deep enough to hear as opening and shutting; try a band-pass in place of the low-pass on one coin of each pair. (3) THE TURN at 129 is the song's best idea and its quietest: make it an event (the drum drops its second and fourth beats there, or the seed's note climbs). (4) THE KEY: echo steps six and on (E, B natural) are 30 dB down but there. (5) A CHORD AS THE SEED for one section: every coin then moves the whole chord a fifth. (3) WAIT: in the two bars before home (159, 160) drum, bass and hat stop; the last off-beat seed's change is alone (-19, -25 dB a bar against -13). (4) CHORD: from bar 161 the seed is G minor (G4 B flat 4 D5, each 6 dB down: 8.6 under the mix where a single seed is 8.0); every coin moves a note a fifth, so the purse walks the chord round the fifths. SCORE 96.60 on both seeds; v2 re-read under the album's seven cuts 94.23. THREE BUILDS. (a) the long seeds at full level: 93.13, six sections: the limiter holds a lone seed about 9 dB, its change came up to it, and the opening stood as loud as the drum (-16 -17 -22 -29 against -15). (b) the long seeds 6 dB down, a one-bar wait: 95.11, home at 0.16. (c) a two-bar wait, the chord 2 dB up: published. WHAT IS WEAK: THE DRUM'S ENTRY at bar 17 no longer counts (0.12; v2 0.19): the bar before it is -34, not silent. THE TURN at 129 still reads under 0.10 and is 0.6 dB lower than v2's, no more: half the drum going is all that marks it. Seven sections is under the range's floor (7.7). Which chords are heard after the first I did not measure; the third step (E minor) is outside the key. I cannot judge whether a chord at home is an arrival or another song walking in.

v4, THE PURSE INSIDE OUT (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 10:50-11:08 GMT). Not heard by me. Three switches (--without-leave, -flip, -fill; all three off is v3 byte for byte). (1) LEAVE: the drum waits whenever the seed changes its place in the bar, to leave as well as to come home. In bars 127 and 128 drum, bass and hat stop and the three purses pay out alone (-20 and -18 dB a bar against -11 to -13). (2) FLIP: while the seed is off the beat the coins change hands (a fourth purse, d: 5 and 3). The five lifts a fifth on the left; the three drops a fourth on the right. The same amounts can be made, so hat and bass do not change; the quick coin's run now falls under the seed where it climbed over it. Read on the purse alone after the first off-beat seed (E flat 4), by sixteenths: 3, B flat 3 on the right (8 dB); 5, B flat 4 on the left (8); 6, F3 right (16); 8, F4 in the middle; 10, F5 left (15). v6, SMALL CHANGE FIRST (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 14:50-15:08 GMT). Not heard by me. The ending pays its last seeds in smaller and smaller coins, and until then nothing in the song had heard a small coin; and every new section but two simply began. Four switches (--without-roll, -gap, -lone, -tumble; all off is v5 byte for byte). (1) ROLL: on beat three of the last bar before a section, a seed on the next section's first note, paid in coins of 3 and 5 thirty-seconds where the purse stays and 3 and 5 sixty-fourths where it is new (bars 32, 48, 64, 80, 112, 144; none where the drum already waits, none before the last section). (2) GAP: the drum gives beat four of that bar to the change (bars 32, 48, 64, 80, 112; at 144 it is already off four). In the finished song, beat three / beat four / the one after, v5 then v6: bar 32 -15/-15/-11 and -13/-15/-11; bar 48 -16/-16/-10 and -12/-18/-11; bar 64 -16/-16/-10 and -13/-21/-11; bar 80 -15/-16/-19 and -12/-18/-19; bar 112 -11/-13/-10 and -11/-14/-10; bar 144 -12/-15/-16 and -13/-14/-15. So beat three is up to 4 dB louder (the roll's seed on the drum) and beat four, with no drum, 0 to 5 dB under what the drum gave it. (3) LONE: the same before the drum first comes and before it comes again (bars 16 and 96), where the roll is alone. At -4 dB it read -15 dBFS on its beat where the lone seeds round it read -18 and the drum's first beat -16 (any lone sound goes to the master's ceiling): louder than everything in the opening. At -10 dB (published) it reads -18 and -24 on its two beats, then the drum at -16; at bar 96 -18 and -22, then the drum at -9. (4) TUMBLE: 'off the beat, up' (bars 145 to 160) was 'off the beat' a tone higher; now the purse turns over at every seed (inside out at 145, 149, 153, 157; the right way at 147, 151, 155, 159). By solo the echo three sixteenths after each seed is 8.0 dB to the right, then 8.0 to the left, in turn. The hat and the bass do not change (the amounts are the same). SCORE 99.62 on both seeds. HOW TO READ THAT: v5 re-read today 98.97, and the only term that moves is recurrence, on the share of the song the scorer hears as returning, whose band stops at 0.70: v5 0.709, the first build (lone rolls at -4) 0.700 and 99.95, published 0.703, the build with no lone rolls 0.715 and 98.41. Thousandths either side of an edge: the points are the scorer's, not a measure of the fills. Its eight sections are the same eight in every build; the drum's first entry at bar 17, which it read at 0.12, it now reads under 0.10. THE SEAMS: bars 13 to 16 read -20.8 for -21.5 (the flurry in bar 16, under Hearing Things' last bar); the last sixteen bars are as they were (-24.1 -23.3 -23.0 -19.2 for -24.0 -23.3 -22.9 -19.1). ALSO READ: the flipped purse's low run (planned since v4): 120 to 250 Hz stands 12.1 and 12.3 dB under the whole in the two turned sections and 11.4 to 12.5 in the others: no build-up, closed.
